subject.title: RFC 0014: Pluggable scheduler seam in gateway

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class scheduler plugin that can become the canonical owner of scheduled-job dispatch while core retains heartbeats and projected run state?
rationale: This adds a permanent plugin kind, runtime API, operator configuration surface, and authority boundary; technical review can validate the RFC, but only maintainers can choose that product contract.

options.title: Accept with rollout gates
options.body: Approve the seam with explicit configuration opt-in, built-in Cron fallback, an implementation issue, compatibility coverage, and validated run-state provenance.

options.title: Narrow the ownership model
options.body: Request a revision where plugins integrate with Cron without disabling core dispatch or becoming the canonical scheduler.

options.title: Keep the HTTP boundary
options.body: Decline a new plugin contract and continue supporting external schedulers through authenticated Gateway HTTP/WebSocket APIs.

recommendation.title: Accept with rollout gates
recommendation.body: Approve the seam with explicit configuration opt-in, built-in Cron fallback, an implementation issue, compatibility coverage, and validated run-state provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: The approved plugin-SDK compatibility RFC is the strongest available ownership signal for deciding a new public plugin contract.
